rationale: Interpreting the tick-period sweep. CheckRun 10db1b327b784fb48711dec936afc73d (exit 0, all three cases passed) evaluated the three comparisons completely and they separate: at 100 ms and at 250 ms the obligation holds (the fresh call returned index 2, which is exactly where entry 33 sits, and the entry at the returned index is the caller's), while at 500 ms it is violated with a complete witness (returned index 4 while entry 33 is at index 2 and index 4 holds entry 35, decided log 22,33,34,35). Together with the two 1000 ms runs this puts the retained band at 100 and 250 ms holding and 500 and 1000 ms violating, so the condition is now receipt-backed rather than resting on one point plus construction feedback. The sweep also exposed a phase difference I am recording rather than smoothing over: the runs that shift report `decided_after_resync` 0 and the new leader's own call unresolved, while the runs that hold report `decided_after_resync` 1 with that call resolved at index 1, so the shift may depend on the origin being re-elected before its re-synchronisation completed rather than on the tick period alone. That is now the sharper open item.

investigations.discriminator: The band is measured (100 and 250 ms hold; 500 and 1000 ms violate) but the sweep confounds two candidate conditions, because the shifting runs also show the origin being re-elected before its re-synchronisation completed (decided index still 0, the new leader's own call unresolved) while the holding runs do not. Separating them is the next judgement-changing step: a run at a tick period where the re-synchronisation completes but the tick is still large, or a construction that holds the origin's re-synchronisation until after its re-election, would decide whether the operative condition is the tick period or the re-election outrunning the re-synchronisation.

knowledge.statement: When a truncation discards entries whose deferred placeholders in `unconfirmed_local` are still queued, those placeholders keep their position in the queue and are consumed by later index advances, so the index reported for a later caller is shifted upward by the number of discarded entries. Retained runs of the same scenario at four tick periods: at 100 and 250 ms the fresh call resolved `ok` with index 2, which is where entry 33 sits; at 500 and 1000 ms it resolved `ok` with index 4 (1000 ms, twice) or 3 and 4 (500 ms, two runs) while entry 33 sat at index 2 or 1 and the returned index held entry 35 - a shift equal to the two buffered entries the truncation discarded.
knowledge.conditions: Actor layer with batch_size 3, three-node cluster, majority quorum, the leader cut off from both followers, the followers taking over with node 3, the origin re-elected explicitly, and a fresh `append_notify` filling the batch with two filler appends. Retained evidence covers tick periods 100, 250, 500 and 1000 ms; the shifting runs all report `decided_after_resync` 0 and the new leader's own call unresolved, the holding runs report `decided_after_resync` 1 and that call resolved, so the tick period is confounded with whether the origin's re-synchronisation completed before its re-election. The internal placeholder queue is unobservable through the public API, so the queue accounting is the mechanism the endpoints imply rather than a direct observation.
knowledge.changed_premise: The tick-period condition is now receipt-backed across a band instead of resting on one exercised point plus construction feedback, and a phase difference between the shifting and holding runs is recorded: the shifting runs (500 and 1000 ms) report the origin's decided index as 0 after the re-synchronisation window and the new leader's own call unresolved, while the holding runs (100 and 250 ms) report decided index 1 and that call resolved at index 1. Whether the operative condition is the tick period or the re-election outrunning the re-synchronisation is therefore not yet separated.

interpretations.rationale: Current account of the second mechanism with a measured band. Deferred writes are tracked as one placeholder per buffered entry in `unconfirmed_local`, `reconcile_unconfirmed` consumes one placeholder per unit of accepted-index advance in queue order, and a placeholder whose buffered ballot no longer matches the current promise is discarded while still consuming its advance; the queue is drained only by that function. When the origin's re-synchronisation discards entries whose placeholders are still queued, the stale placeholders remain ahead of later ones, so a later caller is told an index further along than its entry's position. The retained evidence across four tick periods is: 100 ms and 250 ms hold (the fresh call returned index 2, exactly where entry 33 sits, and that index held the caller's entry), while 500 ms and 1000 ms violate with the same complete witness shape - the call returned an index holding entry 35 while entry 33 sat two positions earlier, matching the two buffered entries the truncation discarded. The sweep also shows a phase difference between the two groups: every shifting run reports the origin's decided index as 0 at the re-synchronisation sample and the new leader's own call unresolved, while every holding run reports decided index 1 and that call resolved at index 1. So while the defect is established and reproducible, the operative condition is not yet isolated between the tick period and the re-election outrunning the re-synchronisation; I am recording that as the account's main open item rather than asserting the tick period as the cause. Impact remains caller-visible in the same way as the arm-order defect but through a different mechanism, and a value check in `drain_notifiers` would mask this symptom without fixing the mis-assignment.
counterevidence: The tick period is confounded with the re-synchronisation outcome in this sweep: the shifting runs are exactly those where the origin's decided index was still 0 when sampled and the new leader's own call had not resolved, so a run that completes the re-synchronisation at a large tick period could hold instead, and the account must not attribute the shift to the tick period alone.
The phase evidence still does not match the construction's intent in the shifting runs, so the moment of the flush and the truncation is inferred from the endpoints rather than observed.
The placeholder queue is unobservable through the public API, so the queue accounting is the explanation the endpoints imply rather than a direct measurement.
A caller that re-reads the decided log at the returned index and compares values is not misled, the mitigation the Superseded variant's documentation already suggests.
limitations: One batch size (3) and a leader origin; follower origins, other batch sizes, and the interaction with the arm-order defect (both can be live in one call) are unmeasured.
Four tick periods, one schedule each at 100, 250 and 500 ms and two at 1000 ms; the boundary between 250 and 500 ms is not located, and the two candidate conditions are not separated.
Three-node cluster, majority quorum, in-process transport; no crash recovery, so nothing here extends to restart-time pending state.
interpretations.joint_history: The first two receipts are the retained finding and its unchanged repeat at a 1000 ms tick period; the third is the revision that parameterised the same scenario on the tick period and added the 100, 250 and 500 ms points. The scenario steps, batch size, election and resend tick counts and the measured quantities are identical across all of them, and the 1000 ms reference case is the same construction in each; the only differences are the tick period and the derived sleeps, which is what lets the receipts be read as one band.
